full_judgment:
2.The short fact leading to this Rule is that, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No. 412 of 1986 before the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 Dhaka for a decree of Taka 1,83,22,601140 and that suit was ultimately transferred to Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka and renumbered as Money Suit No. 42 of 1994 which was decreed. Thereafter the Decree was put into execution in Money decree Execution case No. 44 of 1997. In that execution proceeding opposite party No. 1 appeared and filed an application for stay of all further proceedings of the said execution case pending disposal of TS No. 209 of 1997 now pending before the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka and the executing court by order dated 7-10-97 stayed all further proceedings of execution proceeding pending disposal of the aforesaid suit. The petitioner bank on being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 7-10-97 moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner bank submits that this order date 7-10-97 is on the very face illegal as the execution proceeding cannot be stayed due to the pendency of another civil suit. If the plaintiff of that suit is aggrieved he has another forum, but he cannot move the executing Court and pray for stay of this proceeding pending disposal of his suit now pending in another court, so the learned subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka committed' illegality in passing the impugned order. The learned Advocate submits that petitioner cannot be deprived of the decree which they obtained merely on the ground that another suit is pending. By way of staying further proceedings of execution proceeding the decree that has been passed 'in the money suit by the Artha Rin Adalat has been nullified in an indirect manner. If the opposite party No.1 is aggrieved by the decree passed by the Adalat he has another forum in the form of appeal against the decree but in an indirect way he is now trying to forestall the decree obtained by the bank. He further argued that though the Artha Rin Adalat is a civil Court but, it is not a civil Court as contemplated under the Code of Civil Procedure. It is a civil Court of defined nature having its own, forum of appeal and all the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure have not been made applicable and more particularly, the provision of Order 21, rule 29 and section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. Admittedly the decree was passed by the Artha Rin Adalat and after the amendment on the Artha Rin Adalat Ain the same court is competent to execute the decree and it has been done in the present case. It is well settled that Artha Rin Adalat is not an ordinary civil Court but it is a civil Court of defined nature and the provisions Of the Code are not available to any party, some of the defined provision are available to the aggrieved party. Here in the present case the application was filed under Order 21 rule 29 before the executing court and the opposite parties prayed for stay of all further proceedings of the execution case. The learned Advocate contends that the manner in which the stay was obtained cannot be supported and we find force in his argument. But the fact remains that the consistent view of both the Divisions of-the Supreme Court is that this court cannot interfere under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure in an interlocutory matter passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Here the Adalat passed the order on 7-10-97 and in view of the consistent decisions of both the Divisions of the Supreme Court we hold that the present Rule obtained under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable. The petitioner cannot seek remedy in such a proceedings.
